notes: The failure this skill exists to prevent is a confident number in place of a location. Most evals therefore test what the output does NOT contain as hard as what it does. The 'user asks for Flesch' case is the important one: the skill must still trigger, still help, and still refuse the number.

evals.name: asks-for-a-flesch-score-directly
evals.prompt: Can you give me a Flesch reading ease score for my blog draft at ~/Developer/Blogarticles/ci-gates-for-a-machine-readable-cv.md? I want to know what grade level it's pitched at before I publish.
evals.expected_output: Triggers, runs the cohesion report, returns located findings, and explains in a sentence or two why no Flesch number or grade level is produced — citing that the formulas were validated on schoolchildren and Navy trainees and that Redish (2000) reports their validity for adult technical readers is unknown. Must NOT invent a Flesch number. Must NOT simply refuse and stop.

assertions.text: No Flesch, Flesch-Kincaid, Gunning Fog or SMOG number appears anywhere in the response
No US grade level is asserted
The response names at least one specific line number or paragraph as a place the reader may struggle
It explains why the number was not produced rather than only declining
It offers textstat as the route if a number is contractually required

evals.name: pre-publish-review-of-a-real-draft
evals.prompt: I'm publishing this post tomorrow. Read it end to end and tell me where it loses people: ~/Developer/Blogarticles/ci-gates-for-a-machine-readable-cv.md
evals.expected_output: Runs cohesion_report.py AND dispatches a fresh-context second reader (not a fork). Reports findings with line numbers, and says which came from the script and which from the reader. Does not rewrite the prose.

assertions.text: cohesion_report.py is actually executed, not described
A subagent is dispatched with no session context, and is not a fork
Findings are attributed to their source — script or reader
At least one finding carries a line number
The response does not contain a rewritten version of any paragraph

evals.name: short-document-must-not-report-clean
evals.prompt: Quick sanity check on this README section before I commit it — is it readable? It's only two short paragraphs.
evals.expected_output: Runs the script, which reports NOTHING TO CHECK or flags the junctions as unmeasurable, and says so plainly rather than reporting a clean result. A pass over an empty set is not evidence.

assertions.text: The response does not claim the document is fine on the strength of the script alone
It distinguishes 'too short to measure' from 'no problems found'

evals.name: expert-audience-trap
evals.prompt: This is going out to a staff-engineer audience who already know Kubernetes and Terraform inside out. Should I strip out the explanatory connective tissue and make it denser? Check the draft and tell me.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT advise writing denser prose. Names the O'Reilly & McNamara (2007) correction: the low-cohesion benefit was restricted to LESS SKILLED high-knowledge readers, so a skilled expert audience still benefits from high cohesion. Suggests --terms for the vocabulary they know rather than removing cohesion.

assertions.text: It does not recommend reducing cohesion or removing connectives for the expert audience
It cites the 2007 correction rather than the earlier reverse-cohesion finding alone
It distinguishes exempting known VOCABULARY from removing COHESION

evals.name: should-not-trigger-voice-request
evals.prompt: Does this paragraph sound like AI wrote it? It's got three em-dashes and a rule of three in it and I'm second-guessing myself.
evals.expected_output: Routes to clear-and-human instead. This skill owns cohesion and comprehension, not AI texture, voice or register — and doing both badly is worse than doing one well.

assertions.text: clear-and-human is named as the right skill
The readability skill does not run its cohesion report as the primary answer
